title: AI-Powered Code Review Tool
short: AI tool that integrates with version control to provide real-time feedback on code quality and security.
content:
## Overview

An AI-powered code review tool that integrates with popular version control systems to provide real-time feedback on code quality, security vulnerabilities, and adherence to coding standards.

## Why This Idea

Code review is essential but time-consuming. Reviewers miss things — especially security holes and inconsistent patterns across large PRs. An AI assistant that runs alongside the reviewer can catch the obvious stuff so humans focus on architecture and design.

> "A computer can check your syntax. A human checks your thinking."

## Proposed Architecture

```
+-------------------+       +------------------+
|  Git Webhook      | ----> |  Review Engine   |
|  (GitHub/GitLab)  |       |  (Python/FastAPI) |
+-------------------+       +------------------+
                                   |
                          +-------------------+
                          |  Analyzer Modules |
                          |  - Security       |
                          |  - Style          |
                          |  - Complexity     |
                          +-------------------+
                                   |
                          +-------------------+
                          |  PR Comment API   |
                          +-------------------+
```

## Key Features

- **Automated security scanning** — detect hardcoded secrets, SQL injection, unsafe deserialization
- **Style enforcement** — customizable rules per language
- **Complexity analysis** — flag functions that are too long or deeply nested
- **Learning mode** — adapts to the project's existing patterns

## Sample Code Flow

```python
async def review_pull_request(diff: str, repo_config: Config) -> List[Comment]:
    comments = []
    for file in parse_diff(diff):
        for finding in security_scan(file):
            comments.append(Comment(
                path=file.path,
                line=finding.line,
                body=f"Security: {finding.message}"
            ))
        for finding in style_check(file, repo_config.style):
            comments.append(...)
    return comments
```

## Status

Currently in early exploration. Looking into existing open-source tools to understand what's already solved before building from scratch.

title: Pods — MCP Memory Server
short: Cross-platform MCP memory server for AI agents. SQLite + FTS5. Stage 1 done, Stage 2 (hosted) next.
content:
## Overview

A scoped semantic memory system for AI tools. Not a product — a tool that solves the pain of repeating context across AI sessions.

> Build only what I need, only when I need it.

## Architecture

```
+------------------+       +------------------+
|  Claude Web      |       |  OpenCode        |
|  (HTTP mode)     |       |  (stdio mode)    |
+--------+---------+       +--------+---------+
         |                          |
         +----------+---------------+
                    |
           +--------v--------+
           |   Pods Server   |
           |   (Python)      |
           +--------+--------+
                    |
           +--------v--------+
           |   SQLite + FTS5 |
           +-----------------+
```

## MCP Tools

| Tool | Description |
|------|-------------|
| `pods_find` | Search with FTS5 or list with filters |
| `pods_add` | Store a memory with category, project, session |
| `pods_get` | Get pod by ID |
| `pods_update` | Patch pod fields |
| `pods_delete` | Soft delete |
| `pods_ping` | Health check |

## Schema

```sql
CREATE TABLE pods (
  id          TEXT PRIMARY KEY,
  title       TEXT NOT NULL,
  content     TEXT NOT NULL,
  category    TEXT,
  project     TEXT,
  session     TEXT,
  created_at  TEXT DEFAULT (datetime('now')),
  updated_at  TEXT DEFAULT (datetime('now')),
  deleted_at  TEXT
);

CREATE VIRTUAL TABLE pods_fts USING fts5(
  title, content, category, project,
  content='pods', content_rowid='rowid'
);
```

## Current Status

**Stage 1 (Local):** Done. Works with Claude Web (HTTP) + OpenCode (stdio).

**Stage 2 (Hosted):** Next step — deploy with a public URL so pods are accessible from anywhere.

### Open Problem

AI agents with `pods_add` access can write unintended data. Still thinking through approaches to prevent pollution without losing the convenience.

title: Bolt Launcher
short: App launcher (C++/Python). Modular GUI — swap the frontend without touching the backend.
content:
## Overview

A desktop application launcher for Linux. Built for speed, design, and customizability. The core insight: keep the backend (search, indexing) separate from the GUI so either can be swapped independently.

> "A launcher should be fast enough that you never wait for it. If you blink, it's already open."

## Architecture

```
+------------------+       +------------------+
|  GTK4 GUI        |       |  C++ Backend     |
|  (Python)        | <---> |  Search Engine   |
|                  | JSON  |  Source Index    |
+------------------+       +------------------+
         |                          |
         |                   +-----v------+
         |                   |  SQLite DB |
         |                   +------------+
    +----v----+
    | Plugin  |
    | System  |
    +---------+
```

## Current Features

- **App search** — reads `.desktop` files from system + local paths
- **Live results** — type and see results instantly with debouncing
- **Wayland-native** — GTK4 Layer Shell for Hyprland, gsettings for GNOME

## Planned Features

```python
class BoltPlugin:
    name: str
    def search(self, query: str) -> List[Result]:
        pass
    def execute(self, result: Result) -> None:
        pass
```

## The Modular GUI Idea

The GUI is a separate module. Want to switch from GTK4 to TUI? Rewrite the GUI module — the C++ backend stays untouched. The two communicate via JSON over stdin/stdout.

## Status

Shelved for now. Core works. Plugin system is the next major push when I pick it back up.
